Consider the orthogonal set $U$ below. By adding a new vector $\mathbf x = [x_1,\,x_2,\,x_3]^T,$ extend the set so that it forms an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{R}^3.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275368/assets/2e9982bf5d1cd57f39cdc15d8392495e803e4573b09414e551bdca782b76683a.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of ${U}$ as $\mathbf{u}_1,\, \mathbf{u}_2.$ To extend the given set to an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{R}^3,$ we need to find a third vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275368/assets/e8a2451004886f6f608537f6a306fd2aceccdab78b934f0111d03e92dcd68834.svg) such that

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275368/assets/163b20970f5c0f2a5003cfe8a8f556d7867cecc6f682cb98e2c029bfac8dffb0.svg)

So, we consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system above and reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns ($1$st and $3$rd). This means $x_2$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get $x_3=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general solution is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275368/assets/8ab2d8e20b41d277d18616e602e1c7d0cff23ba740258c5fbc0c04f283f8c313.svg)

Setting $x_2=1,$ we obtain the vector 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275368/assets/779790aeb1fad427347d57850dc157688190eab6c459076a5f04161432ea051c.svg)

Therefore, an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is
